controls.title: BES Cyber System Categorization
controls.description: Inventory the cyber systems that support the bulk power system and rank each by how badly its loss or misuse would hurt grid reliability, so protections scale to that impact.

controls.title: Identify and categorize BES Cyber Systems
controls.description: Run a written process that finds every in-scope cyber system and sorts it into high, medium, or low impact against the bright-line criteria, revisiting the results at least every 15 months.

controls.title: CIP Senior Manager approval of categorization
controls.description: Get the senior accountable manager (or a delegate) to sign off on the system list and impact ratings at least every 15 months, even when a site turns up no in-scope systems.

controls.title: Security Management Controls
controls.description: Set up governance that makes clear who owns cyber protection of grid systems and holds them accountable, so security controls are applied consistently and sustained over time.

controls.title: Documented cyber security policies
controls.description: Keep written cyber security policies covering each CIP topic area, approved by the senior accountable manager, and re-review and re-approve them at least every 15 months.

controls.title: Low impact BES Cyber System plans
controls.description: For low impact assets, put written plans in place for awareness, physical and electronic access, incident handling, transient device use, and defenses against malicious code.

controls.title: CIP Senior Manager identification
controls.description: Name a specific person as the accountable CIP senior manager and record any change of that person within 30 days.

controls.title: Delegation of authority
controls.description: Record, by name or role, anyone the senior manager authorizes to act on their behalf, have the senior manager approve it, and refresh the record within 30 days of changes.

controls.title: Personnel and Training
controls.description: Reduce insider-driven risk to grid systems by screening, training, and keeping security-aware everyone who gets logical or physical access to in-scope assets.

controls.title: Security Awareness Program
controls.description: Run a written security awareness program and push reminders or awareness content to staff at least every calendar quarter.

controls.title: Training Program
controls.description: Provide cyber security training to everyone who holds approved logical access or unescorted physical access to in-scope systems, tailored to what they do.

controls.title: Role-based training content
controls.description: Cover policies, access controls, visitor handling, incident response, recovery, and protected-information handling in training, scoped to each person's job.

controls.title: Train before access
controls.description: Make sure people finish their training before they are given logical or unescorted physical access, unless an emergency exception applies.

controls.title: 15-month refresher training
controls.description: Retrain everyone who holds access no less often than once every 15 calendar months.

controls.title: Personnel Risk Assessment Program
controls.description: Run a written background-screening program that people must pass before getting, and while keeping, logical or unescorted physical access to in-scope systems.

controls.title: Access Management Program
controls.description: Run a written program governing how people request, receive, and keep logical or unescorted physical entry to in-scope systems, and how approvals are tracked.

controls.title: Authorization based on need
controls.description: Grant logical access, unescorted physical access, and access to protected system information only when a documented business reason supports it.

controls.title: Quarterly access verification
controls.description: Every quarter, confirm that each person holding active access still appears on the list of approved individuals.

controls.title: 15-month privilege review
controls.description: At least every 15 months, confirm each user's privileges are accurate and no broader than their job actually requires.

controls.title: BES Cyber Information access review
controls.description: At least every 15 months, confirm that the people who can reach repositories of protected system information still need that access.

controls.title: Access Revocation Program
controls.description: Run a written process to pull access promptly when someone leaves, moves to a new role, or no longer needs their current permissions.

controls.title: Electronic Security Perimeter(s)
controls.description: Control network access to grid cyber systems by wrapping them in a defined, managed network boundary that guards against compromise.

controls.title: Electronic Security Perimeter
controls.description: Place every in-scope system that talks over a routable network inside a defined, documented security perimeter.

controls.title: Define Electronic Security Perimeters
controls.description: Draw a documented network security boundary around every in-scope system that communicates using a routable protocol.

controls.title: Identify Electronic Access Points
controls.description: Route all outside routable traffic through named access points sitting on the perimeter, so there are no undocumented paths in or out.

controls.title: Deny by default inbound and outbound
controls.description: Configure perimeter access points to allow only traffic with a documented business need in each direction and block everything else.

controls.title: Dial-up authentication
controls.description: Require authentication on any dial-up connection into in-scope systems wherever the equipment supports it.

controls.title: Malicious communication detection at EAPs
controls.description: At perimeter access points guarding high and medium impact control center systems, watch inbound and outbound traffic for known or suspected malicious activity.

controls.title: Remote Access Management
controls.description: Secure every interactive remote session into in-scope systems with multi-factor login and an encrypted connection.

controls.title: Intermediate System for remote access
controls.description: Force all interactive remote sessions through a jump host or similar intermediary so outside users never reach protected systems directly.

controls.title: Encrypt remote access sessions
controls.description: Encrypt interactive remote sessions along the path from the user's device to the intermediary system.

controls.title: Multi-factor for remote access
controls.description: Require multi-factor login for every interactive remote session, so a stolen password alone is not enough to reach protected systems from outside.

controls.title: Physical Security of BES Cyber Systems
controls.description: Guard in-scope cyber systems against physical tampering by putting a documented physical security plan in place.

controls.title: Physical Security Plan
controls.description: Write and carry out physical security plans that keep unauthorized people away from in-scope systems and the devices that sit alongside them.

controls.title: Visitor Control Program
controls.description: Run a visitor program that keeps visitors escorted at all times inside protected areas and records their entry and exit, manually or automatically.

controls.title: Physical Access Control System Maintenance and Testing
controls.description: Maintain and periodically test the badge readers, locks, and other physical access control systems to confirm they work as designed.

controls.title: System Security Management
controls.description: Harden and manage in-scope systems through a set of technical, operational, and procedural safeguards that reduce the chance of compromise.

controls.title: Ports and Services
controls.description: Disable network ports and services that are not needed, keeping open only those with a confirmed business purpose where the device allows.

controls.title: Security Patch Management
controls.description: Run a written patching process that tracks, reviews, and installs security updates for in-scope systems.

controls.title: Patch source identification
controls.description: For each in-scope asset, record where its security updates come from so new releases can be tracked.

controls.title: 35-day patch evaluation
controls.description: Check newly released security updates for relevance no less than once every 35 days.

controls.title: Apply, plan, or mitigate within 35 days
controls.description: Within 35 days of deciding an update applies, either install it or write or update a dated mitigation plan with interim safeguards and a target finish date.

controls.title: Execute mitigation plans
controls.description: Carry out patch mitigation plans by their target dates, or get the senior manager or delegate to approve any change to the plan.

controls.title: Malicious Code Prevention
controls.description: Use anti-malware or equivalent controls to prevent, catch, or discourage malicious code on every in-scope asset.

controls.title: Security Event Monitoring
controls.description: Capture security logs from in-scope systems so incidents can be spotted and investigated afterward.

controls.title: Log security events
controls.description: Record security-relevant activity on in-scope systems, including successful and failed logins and any detected malicious behavior, to support detection and later investigation.

controls.title: Alert on security events
controls.description: Raise alerts for security events the organization flags as alert-worthy, such as malware detections and, where supported, failures of logging itself.

controls.title: 90-day log retention
controls.description: Keep relevant security logs for a minimum of 90 days in a row, barring emergency exceptions.

controls.title: 15-day log review
controls.description: For high impact control center systems, review a summary or sample of logs at least every 15 days to catch incidents that went unnoticed.

controls.title: System Access Controls
controls.description: Require login for interactive use, control shared and default accounts, apply password rules, and restrict repeated failed login attempts.

controls.title: Enforce authentication of interactive access
controls.description: Make users authenticate before interactive access to in-scope systems, wherever the system supports it.

controls.title: Inventory default and generic accounts
controls.description: List the enabled default and generic accounts on each asset or asset group, so none of these non-personal logins go untracked.

controls.title: Identify shared-account users
controls.description: Keep a record of which people are allowed to use each shared account, so activity under that login can be traced back to individuals.

controls.title: Change known default passwords
controls.description: Replace vendor default passwords on assets before or when they go into service, as far as the device permits.

controls.title: Password strength parameters
controls.description: Set password rules requiring at least eight characters and three character types, or the most the system can support.

controls.title: 15-month password changes
controls.description: Make users change passwords, or be required to, at least every 15 months where the system supports it.

controls.title: Limit or alert on failed authentication
controls.description: Cap failed login attempts or send an alert once failures pass a set threshold, where the system supports it.

controls.title: Incident Reporting and Response Planning
controls.description: Reduce harm to grid reliability from cyber incidents by establishing how the organization detects, handles, and reports them.

controls.title: Cyber Security Incident Response Plan
controls.description: Write incident response plans that explain how cyber incidents are recognized, classified, and responded to, including roles and reporting.

controls.title: Cyber Security Incident Response Plan Implementation and Testing
controls.description: Put incident response plans into practice and exercise each one, through a real event or a drill, at least every 15 months.

controls.title: Cyber Security Incident Response Plan Review and Update
controls.description: Revise incident response plans after lessons learned from incidents or tests and whenever the protected systems change.

controls.title: Recovery Plans for BES Cyber Systems
controls.description: Make sure grid functions supported by cyber systems can be restored after an outage or attack by keeping workable recovery plans.

controls.title: Recovery Plan Specifications
controls.description: Write recovery plans spelling out when they kick in, who does what, how backups are taken and stored, and the steps to restore in-scope systems.

controls.title: Recovery Plan Implementation and Testing
controls.description: Carry out and exercise each recovery plan, through real recovery or a test, at least every 15 months.

controls.title: Recovery Plan Review and Update
controls.description: Keep recovery plans current, folding in lessons learned and any changes to the systems they cover.

controls.title: Configuration Change Management and Vulnerability Assessments
controls.description: Stop and catch unapproved changes to in-scope systems through baseline-driven change control and periodic vulnerability assessments.

controls.title: Configuration Change Management
controls.description: Record a known-good configuration for in-scope systems and approve and document any change that departs from it.

controls.title: Develop baseline configurations
controls.description: Capture a baseline for each asset or group listing OS or firmware, installed commercial and open-source software, custom code, open ports, and patches applied.

controls.title: Authorize baseline changes
controls.description: Approve and record any change that alters an asset's documented baseline before or as it happens.

controls.title: Update baselines within 30 days
controls.description: Bring the baseline record up to date within 30 days after a change is finished.

controls.title: Verify security controls after changes
controls.description: When a baseline changes, identify which perimeter and system security controls it could affect, confirm they still work, and record the outcome.

controls.title: Test changes before production (high impact)
controls.description: For high impact systems, test changes in a representative test setup or by another documented method before production, noting how the test setup differs.

controls.title: Configuration Monitoring
controls.description: Check in-scope systems for unapproved deviations from their recorded baselines at least once every 35 days, and follow up on anything found.

controls.title: 35-day unauthorized-change monitoring
controls.description: For high impact systems, compare configurations against baselines at least every 35 days and record and investigate any unauthorized differences found.

controls.title: Vulnerability Assessments
controls.description: Assess in-scope systems for vulnerabilities, through a document review or hands-on scan, at least every 15 months.

controls.title: 15-month vulnerability assessment
controls.description: Perform a vulnerability assessment, either desk-based or hands-on, no less than once every 15 months.

controls.title: 36-month active assessment (high impact)
controls.description: For high impact systems, run a hands-on vulnerability assessment in test or production at least every 36 months where feasible.

controls.title: Assess new assets before connection
controls.description: For high impact systems, scan new assets for vulnerabilities before putting them into production.

controls.title: Document assessment results and action plans
controls.description: Write up assessment findings along with a remediation or mitigation plan and target dates, and track progress until closed.

controls.title: Information Protection
controls.description: Keep sensitive information about grid cyber systems out of unauthorized hands by putting information protection controls in place.

controls.title: Information Protection Program
controls.description: Run a written program that identifies sensitive system information and sets rules for how it is handled, stored, and shared.

controls.title: BES Cyber Asset Reuse and Disposal
controls.description: Before reusing or disposing of in-scope assets, follow written procedures to wipe or destroy media so sensitive system data cannot be recovered.

controls.title: Communications between Control Centers
controls.description: Protect real-time operational and assessment data exchanged between control centers from disclosure and tampering under documented plans.

controls.title: Plan to protect Control Center communication links
controls.description: Maintain and follow a written plan that protects real-time data moving between control centers from snooping and alteration, naming the safeguards used, where responsibility hands off, and who owns each piece.

controls.title: Supply Chain Risk Management
controls.description: Manage cyber risk introduced through vendors and the products and services bought for grid cyber systems.

controls.title: Supply chain risk management plan
controls.description: For high and medium impact systems, write supply chain risk plans covering vendor breach notification, joint incident response, verification of software integrity and origin, and control of vendor remote access.

controls.title: Implement the supply chain plan
controls.description: Apply the supply chain risk plans when buying products and services for in-scope systems.

controls.title: 15-month CIP Senior Manager review
controls.description: Have the senior manager or delegate review and approve the supply chain risk plans at least every 15 months.

controls.title: Physical Security of Transmission Stations and Substations
controls.description: Find the substations and their control centers whose physical loss could destabilize or split the grid, then protect them against physical attack.

controls.title: Risk assessment of critical stations
controls.description: Periodically study the transmission network to pinpoint which substations, if knocked out or damaged, would trigger grid instability, islanding, or cascading outages.

controls.title: Threat and vulnerability evaluation
controls.description: For each critical site identified, assess the physical threats it faces and the weaknesses an attacker could exploit.

controls.title: Physical security plan
controls.description: Create and carry out a written physical security plan for each critical site, with protective or resilience measures, coordination with law enforcement, and a schedule for upgrades.
